writeup.key_factor: Los Angeles is the NHL's only winless team (0-4-2) with the league's weakest attack (2.00 goals/game) and penalty kill (61.9%). The goalie matchup is confirmed and lopsided: Logan Thompson (4-2, .910 SV%) starts for Washington against Darcy Kuemper (0-3-1, 4.53 GAA, .847 SV%). Washington is 5-3 and 4-1 at home.
writeup.risk: The Kings' underlying chances (2.91 expected goals for per game) are better than their record, so positive regression is the main threat. Washington also allows a high shot volume. If the price drifts past -162 the edge is gone and the play should be passed.

writeup.key_factor: Toronto plays the second night of a back-to-back on the road, without John Tavares (7 points in 7 games) and Chris Tanev, and starts Anthony Stolarz (.875 SV%) while Sergei Bobrovsky stays home. Columbus is rested at home with Jet Greaves coming off a 30-save shutout, and the Jackets have earned points in 7 of the last 9 head-to-head meetings, winning 3 of the last 4 in Columbus.
writeup.risk: The model edge is thin at this price — this is a probability play, not a value play. Toronto's special teams are elite (power play 28%, penalty kill 97%) and Columbus is missing key defensemen (Provorov, Fabbro, Lundestrom). At -155 or worse, pass.
